title: Hungary: History, Geography, Culture & Heritage
description: A 60-question grand master assessment on Hungary covering the Arpad dynasty, Ottoman wars, 1956 Revolution, Budapest landmarks, Lake Balaton, Hungarian inventions, and folklore.

questions.question: Who was the first crowned King of Hungary, crowned around the year 1000 or 1001?
questions.explanation: Saint Stephen I founded the Kingdom of Hungary and introduced Christianity to the realm.

questions.question: Which major European river divides the Hungarian capital into Buda and Pest?
questions.explanation: The Danube flows through central Budapest, separating hilly Buda from flat Pest.

questions.question: What is the largest freshwater lake in Central Europe, often called the Hungarian Sea?
questions.explanation: Lake Balaton covers approximately 592 square kilometers and is a primary resort destination.

questions.question: Which spice made from dried and ground chili peppers is the hallmark seasoning of Hungarian cuisine?
questions.explanation: Paprika is essential to traditional dishes like goulash, pörkölt, and paprikás.

questions.question: What is the currency of Hungary?
questions.explanation: The Hungarian Forint (HUF) is the official currency of Hungary.

questions.question: In what year was the historic Golden Bull (Aranybulla) issued by King Andrew II limiting royal powers?
questions.explanation: The Golden Bull of 1222 was one of the earliest constitutional documents in Europe.

questions.question: Which Hungarian architect designed the iconic neo-Gothic Hungarian Parliament Building in Budapest?
questions.explanation: Imre Steindl designed the grand Parliament building on the Pest bank of the Danube, completed in 1904.

questions.question: In which year did the anti-Soviet Hungarian Revolution and Freedom Fight take place?
questions.explanation: The Hungarian Revolution began on October 23, 1956, and was brutally suppressed by Soviet forces in November.

questions.question: Which famous 15th-century Hungarian monarch was celebrated as "the Just" and established the Black Army?
questions.explanation: King Matthias Corvinus made Hungary a center of Renaissance art and humanism.

questions.question: What iconic suspension bridge was the first permanent stone bridge to span the Danube connecting Buda and Pest?
questions.explanation: The Széchenyi Chain Bridge opened in 1849, championed by Count István Széchenyi.

questions.question: Which Hungarian biochemist isolated Vitamin C and won the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine?
questions.explanation: Albert Szent-Györgyi extracted ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) from paprika in Szeged.

questions.question: In what year was the decisive Battle of Mohács fought against the Ottoman Empire?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Mohács in 1526 resulted in the defeat of King Louis II and the partition of Hungary.

questions.question: What famous fortress city successfully repelled the Ottoman siege of 1552 led by István Dobó?
questions.explanation: The defenders of Eger Castle, including the brave women of Eger, repelled an overwhelming Ottoman army.

questions.question: Which renowned Hungarian inventor created the 3-D combination puzzle cube in 1974?
questions.explanation: Ernő Rubik invented the Rubik's Cube, which became the world's best-selling puzzle toy.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in Hungary, located in the Mátra mountain range?
questions.explanation: Kékes reaches an elevation of 1,014 meters above sea level.

questions.question: Which sweet botrytized dessert wine from northeastern Hungary was famously called the "Wine of Kings, King of Wines"?
questions.explanation: Tokaji Aszú is made from noble-rot affected grapes in the historic Tokaj wine region.

questions.question: Which Hungarian polymath is known as the father of modern game theory and digital computer architecture?
questions.explanation: John von Neumann (Neumann János) formulated computer architecture and foundation of game theory.

questions.question: What is the elevation of Mount Kékes, the highest point in Hungary, in meters?
questions.explanation: Mount Kékes stands at exactly 1,014 meters (3,327 ft) in the Mátra range.

questions.question: What grand Budapest square features the Millennium Monument commemorating the 1000th anniversary of the Magyar conquest?
questions.explanation: Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) features the Seven Chieftains and statues of historic Hungarian rulers.

questions.question: Which Hungarian journalist invented the modern commercial ballpoint pen patented in 1938?
questions.explanation: László Bíró invented the ballpoint pen, still called "biro" in many countries.

questions.question: What medieval treaty signed in 1920 in the Grand Trianon Palace stripped Hungary of over two-thirds of its pre-WWI territory?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Trianon in 1920 partitioned historic Greater Hungary following the First World War.

questions.question: Which Hungarian composer wrote the Hungarian Rhapsodies and the Faust Symphony?
questions.explanation: Franz Liszt (Liszt Ferenc) was a virtuoso pianist and premier Romantic-era composer.

questions.question: What is the name of the distinctive red blend wine from the Eger region literally translating to "Bull's Blood"?
questions.explanation: Egri Bikavér is Hungary's most celebrated traditional red cuvée wine.

questions.question: In what year was the Budapest Millennium Underground (Line M1), the oldest electrified underground railway in continental Europe, opened?
questions.explanation: The M1 metro line opened in 1896 for the Millennium celebrations of the Hungarian state.

questions.question: Which Hungarian physician demonstrated in 1847 that handwashing with chlorinated lime drastically reduced puerperal childbed fever?
questions.explanation: Ignaz Semmelweis is celebrated today as the pioneer of antiseptic procedures.

questions.question: Which castle in Budapest sits on the southern tip of Castle Hill and served as the historic royal seat?
questions.explanation: Buda Castle (Budavári Palota) is a UNESCO World Heritage site dominating the Buda skyline.

questions.question: Which mythical bird from Hungarian mythology is said to have guided the ancient Magyars to the Carpathian Basin?
questions.explanation: The Turul is a divine falcon-like bird and national symbol in Hungarian myth.

questions.question: Who was the Hungarian prime minister during the 1956 revolution who declared Hungarian neutrality from the Warsaw Pact?
questions.explanation: Imre Nagy led the revolutionary government and was executed in 1958 following Soviet invasion.

questions.question: Which famous thermal bath complex in Budapest's City Park is one of the largest medicinal baths in Europe?
questions.explanation: The Széchenyi Medicinal Bath features 21 indoor and outdoor thermal pools with neo-Baroque architecture.

questions.question: How many sovereign countries share an international land border with Hungary?
questions.explanation: Hungary borders Austria, Slovakia, Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia.

questions.question: Which Hungarian mathematician was renowned for authoring over 1,500 research papers and establishing the "Erdős number"?
questions.explanation: Paul Erdős collaborated with hundreds of mathematicians around the globe during his nomadic career.

questions.question: What is the traditional Hungarian open-air national park and vast grassland steppe in eastern Hungary called?
questions.explanation: The Puszta in Hortobágy National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.

questions.question: Which 19th-century Hungarian national poet wrote the "Nemzeti Dal" (National Song) that sparked the 1848 Hungarian Revolution?
questions.explanation: Sándor Petőfi read his revolutionary poem on the steps of the National Museum on March 15, 1848.

questions.question: Which Hungarian-American biochemist co-developed modified mRNA technology recognized with the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine?
questions.explanation: Katalin Karikó received the Nobel Prize with Drew Weissman for groundbreaking mRNA discoveries.

questions.question: What Hungarian chess grandmaster is universally considered the greatest female chess player in history, having defeated Garry Kasparov?
questions.explanation: Judit Polgár achieved the Grandmaster title at age 15 and entered the world's top 10 overall chess rating.

questions.question: In what year did the Hungarian national football team ("Mighty Magyars") famously defeat England 6-3 at Wembley Stadium?
questions.explanation: The "Match of the Century" in 1953 saw Ferenc Puskás and Hungary crush England's home record.

questions.question: What legendary Hungarian striker served as captain of the 1950s Golden Team and gave his name to the FIFA best goal award?
questions.explanation: Ferenc Puskás scored 84 goals in 85 international matches and later starred for Real Madrid.

questions.question: Which historic coronation town and seat of the Hungarian Catholic Primate boasts Hungary's largest basilica church?
questions.explanation: Esztergom Basilica sits high above the Danube bend and is the monumental mother church of Hungary.

questions.question: Which 19th-century Hungarian leader spearheaded economic modernization and built the Danube steam navigation network?
questions.explanation: Count István Széchenyi is honored as "the Greatest Hungarian" (a Legnagyobb Magyar).

questions.question: What traditional Hungarian chimney cake coated with sugar, walnuts, or cinnamon is baked over charcoal?
questions.explanation: Kürtőskalács originated in Transylvania (Székely Land) and is a beloved festival pastry.

questions.question: Which city in southwestern Hungary was named a European Capital of Culture in 2010 and is noted for Early Christian necropolises?
questions.explanation: Pécs boasts 4th-century Roman tombs, Turkish mosques, and the Zsolnay porcelain quarter.

questions.question: How many administrative counties (megyék) make up the territory of Hungary, excluding Budapest?
questions.explanation: Hungary is subdivided into 19 counties plus the capital city of Budapest.

questions.question: What layered sponge cake with chocolate buttercream topped with caramelized sugar slices was invented by a Budapest confectioner in 1884?
questions.explanation: József Dobos introduced his namesake torte at the 1885 National General Exhibition in Budapest.

questions.question: Which Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction and co-authored the Einstein-Szilard letter to FDR in 1939?
questions.explanation: Leo Szilard patented the idea of nuclear chain reaction and helped launch the Manhattan Project.

questions.question: What famous fairytale-like panoramic terrace on the Buda side of the Danube was built in neo-Romanesque style between 1895 and 1902?
questions.explanation: Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) features seven towers representing the seven Magyar tribes.

questions.question: Which large river is the longest tributary of the Danube and flows right through the Great Hungarian Plain (Alföld)?
questions.explanation: The Tisza River traverses northeastern and eastern Hungary through Tokaj and Szeged.

questions.question: Which Hungarian author won the 2002 Nobel Prize in Literature for his Holocaust semi-autobiographical novel "Fatelessness"?
questions.explanation: Imre Kertész received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2002 for writing that upholds fragile human experience against barbarian tyranny.

questions.question: In what year was the Austro-Hungarian Compromise (Ausgleich) established creating the Dual Monarchy?
questions.explanation: The Compromise of 1867 established the Austro-Hungarian Empire with Franz Joseph I as king.

questions.question: Which Hungarian city in eastern Hungary is famously known as the "Calvinist Rome" due to its historic Protestant College?
questions.explanation: Debrecen was the ecclesiastical capital of Hungarian Protestantism and twice national capital.

questions.question: What Hungarian invention by Tivadar Puskás in 1876 transformed telecommunications networks worldwide?
questions.explanation: Tivadar Puskás conceptualized the telephone exchange and the Telefon Hírmondó news service.

questions.question: Which Hungarian national holiday celebrated on March 15 commemorates the Revolution of 1848?
questions.explanation: March 15 celebrates the 1848 civic revolution and freedom fight led by Lajos Kossuth and Sándor Petőfi.

questions.question: Which thermal lake near Lake Balaton is the second largest biological thermal lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Hévíz has natural warm mineral waters renewed every few days from underwater thermal springs.

questions.question: What famous traditional herbal digestif liqueur produced in Hungary since 1790 comes in a round dark-green bottle?
questions.explanation: Zwack Unicum is a proprietary digestif formulated with more than 40 medicinal herbs and spices.

questions.question: In what year was the Holy Crown of Hungary returned to the Hungarian people from the United States?
questions.explanation: President Jimmy Carter returned the Holy Crown of Saint Stephen to Budapest on January 6, 1978.

questions.question: Which prominent 20th-century Hungarian composer integrated authentic folk song field recordings into modern classical music?
questions.explanation: Béla Bartók traveled the Carpathian countryside recording authentic peasant music with a phonograph.

questions.question: What Hungarian fruit brandy distilled strictly from Hungarian-grown fruits (plums, apricots, pears) is an EU protected spirit?
questions.explanation: Pálinka is Hungary's traditional national distilled fruit brandy protected by geographical origin.

questions.question: Which Gothic church in Buda Castle was the site of the coronation of the last two Hungarian kings?
questions.explanation: Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) features iconic Zsolnay ceramic roof tiles and Gothic spires.

questions.question: Who served as regent of the Kingdom of Hungary between 1920 and 1944 during the interwar era?
questions.explanation: Admiral Miklós Horthy served as Regent of Hungary throughout the interwar and early WWII period.

questions.question: Which Hungarian-born British physicist received the 1971 Nobel Prize in Physics for inventing holography?
questions.explanation: Dennis Gabor (Gábor Dénes) invented holography in 1947, revolutionizing optical recording.

questions.question: In what year did Hungary officially join the European Union alongside nine other accession states?
questions.explanation: Hungary joined the European Union on May 1, 2004, in the largest single enlargement.
